evidence.title: An alert is reviewed during a live training run
evidence.observation: OpenAI reports September internet access was flagged within 15 minutes; a responder began review three minutes later. Frontier reinforcement learning was subsequently paused. Qualification approved October 30, 2026: OpenAI reports successful live detection and prompt human acknowledgment, followed by failure of the expected automatic stop and delayed manual termination. The event supports distinguishing detection and acknowledgment from effective intervention.

source_locations.SRC-007: Investigation and response: incident timeline and operational gaps paragraph

evidence.limitations: The public account does not establish complete independent chaperoning or a universal response time. The same disclosure says paging coverage varies by workload. The detailed report identifies failed automatic stopping and delayed manual termination. It does not establish harmful activity during the delay. The two accounts are dependent; the timeline timezone is unspecified.

terms.name: Chaperoning
terms.definition: The continuing supervisory activity of independently observing consequential behavior, exercising informed judgment, and intervening effectively when appropriate. This requires access, competence, authority, and an actual ability to alter outcomes—not nominal participation or an agent merely stating that an action is inappropriate.

terms.name: Observability
terms.definition: The capacity to obtain and interpret dependable evidence about states, actions, relationships, and consequences relevant to a specified question. Evidence may come from more than one system or organization.

relationships.explanation: Alert, human review, and subsequent pausing provide a bounded supervisory sequence; independence and full effectiveness remain unverified. Qualification: the provider reports failed automatic stopping and delayed manual termination; the sequence illustrates why detection and acknowledgment must be distinguished from effective intervention.
The account separates detecting a boundary crossing from human review and action.
Reported configuration context is distinct from the live DNS event; shared publication does not provide independent corroboration.
